newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firmer on strong jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firmer on strong jobs data.

text.p: Mexican peso contracts closed firmer across the board for the second session in a row on Thursday.
Brokers jumped in to sell dollars to invest in the local stock and money markets after lower than expected unemployment figures were released, dealers said.

"Dollars flooded the market. Players are very optimistic over the bourse, the interest rates and jobs," a trader said. The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed trade 2.2 and 2.6 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8530/7.8580 and 7.8440/7.8490 per dollar.

Mexico's Statistics Institute (INEGI) announced a June open unemployment rate of 3.4 percent, considerably below an average of 3.92 percent predicted in the latest Reuters survey of economic forecasts.

Dealers said peso flows had pushed up the bourse's blue chip IPC index by 51.78 points to 4,839.21 points and brought down overnight Cetes rates in the secondary money market by 125 basis points to 18.25 percent. Same-day peso contracts closed mid-morning 7.6 centavos firmer at 7.8460/7.8490 per dollar.
Dealers did not see the peso strengthening much further. "After breaking through at 7.8500 per dollar, the next target is at 7.8000, but I feel it will stay where it is," a trader said.
